# Purpose

This document determines the sample size for estimating the mean monthly number of pages printed or photocopied by students in the simulated finite population of 10,000 Wits University students.

The primary design is stratified random sampling without replacement, using faculty as the stratum. Neyman allocation is used because the stratum-specific population standard deviations are known from the simulated finite population.

The SRSWOR calculation is included as a benchmark.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

# Known finite-population quantities

The following quantities come from the population generated with random seed 4102.

```{r known-values}
N <- 10000
baseline_mean <- 111.54
overall_variance <- 3900.87
overall_sd <- 62.46

faculty <- c(
  "Commerce, Law and Management",
  "Engineering and the Built Environment",
  "Health Sciences",
  "Humanities",
  "Science"
)

N_h <- c(2500, 2000, 1700, 2300, 1500)
S_h <- c(52.53, 37.28, 61.17, 80.76, 42.60)

known_values <- data.frame(
  faculty = faculty,
  N_h = N_h,
  W_h = N_h / N,
  S_h = S_h
)

known_values
```

# Confidence level and required precision

A 95% confidence level is used, so the normal critical value is 1.96.

The required confidence-interval half-width is 5% of the baseline population mean.

```{r precision}
z <- qnorm(0.975)

E <- 0.05 * baseline_mean

cat("95% critical value =", round(z, 4), "\n")
cat("Baseline population mean =", baseline_mean, "pages per month\n")
cat("Required half-width (5% of baseline) =", round(E, 3), "pages\n")
```

Thus, the target half-width is approximately 5.58 pages per student per month.

# SRSWOR benchmark sample size

For estimating a finite-population mean under SRSWOR, the sample size is



```{r srs-sample-size}
n_srs_raw <- (N * z^2 * overall_variance) /
  (E^2 * (N - 1) + z^2 * overall_variance)

n_srs <- ceiling(n_srs_raw)

cat("Unrounded SRSWOR sample size =", round(n_srs_raw, 3), "\n")
cat("Minimum SRSWOR sample size =", n_srs, "\n")
```

# Stratified sample size under Neyman allocation


```{r helper-functions}
allocate_neyman <- function(n_total, N_h, S_h) {
  raw <- n_total * (N_h * S_h) / sum(N_h * S_h)
  alloc <- floor(raw)
  remainder <- n_total - sum(alloc)

  if (remainder > 0) {
    order_fraction <- order(raw - alloc, decreasing = TRUE)
    alloc[order_fraction[seq_len(remainder)]] <-
      alloc[order_fraction[seq_len(remainder)]] + 1
  }

  alloc
}

strat_variance <- function(n_h, N_h, S_h) {
  W_h <- N_h / sum(N_h)

  sum(
    W_h^2 *
      (1 - n_h / N_h) *
      (S_h^2 / n_h)
  )
}

strat_halfwidth <- function(n_total, N_h, S_h, z = qnorm(0.975)) {
  n_h <- allocate_neyman(n_total, N_h, S_h)
  z * sqrt(strat_variance(n_h, N_h, S_h))
}

find_min_strat_n <- function(E_target, N_h, S_h, z = qnorm(0.975)) {
  for (n in seq_along(seq_len(sum(N_h)))) {
    if (n < length(N_h)) next

    n_h <- allocate_neyman(n, N_h, S_h)

    if (all(n_h >= 1)) {
      hw <- z * sqrt(strat_variance(n_h, N_h, S_h))

      if (hw <= E_target) {
        return(list(
          n = n,
          n_h = n_h,
          halfwidth = hw,
          variance = strat_variance(n_h, N_h, S_h)
        ))
      }
    }
  }

  stop("No feasible sample size found.")
}
```

Now solve for the minimum total sample size satisfying the required 5% precision bound.

```{r minimum-stratified-n}
strat_result <- find_min_strat_n(
  E_target = E,
  N_h = N_h,
  S_h = S_h,
  z = z
)

n_strat <- strat_result$n
n_h_min <- strat_result$n_h

cat("Minimum stratified sample size =", n_strat, "\n")
cat("Achieved half-width =", round(strat_result$halfwidth, 3), "pages\n")
cat("Estimated variance of stratified mean =",
    round(strat_result$variance, 4), "\n")
cat("Estimated SE =",
    round(sqrt(strat_result$variance), 4), "pages\n")
```

# Neyman allocation of the minimum sample

```{r minimum-allocation}
allocation_minimum <- data.frame(
  faculty = faculty,
  N_h = N_h,
  S_h = S_h,
  n_h = n_h_min
)

allocation_minimum$inclusion_probability <-
  allocation_minimum$n_h / allocation_minimum$N_h

allocation_minimum$weight <-
  allocation_minimum$N_h / allocation_minimum$n_h

allocation_minimum
cat("Total allocated =", sum(allocation_minimum$n_h), "\n")
```

# Adjustment for anticipated non-response


```{r nonresponse}
nonresponse_rate <- 0.10

n_final <- ceiling(n_strat / (1 - nonresponse_rate))

cat("Minimum completed sample required =", n_strat, "\n")
cat("Assumed non-response rate =", nonresponse_rate * 100, "%\n")
cat("Initial sample after non-response adjustment =", n_final, "\n")
```

The non-response-adjusted total is also allocated across the five strata using Neyman allocation.

```{r final-allocation}
n_h_final <- allocate_neyman(n_final, N_h, S_h)

final_allocation <- data.frame(
  faculty = faculty,
  N_h = N_h,
  S_h = S_h,
  n_h = n_h_final
)

final_allocation$inclusion_probability <-
  final_allocation$n_h / final_allocation$N_h

final_allocation$sampling_weight <-
  final_allocation$N_h / final_allocation$n_h

final_allocation
cat("Final total sample =", sum(final_allocation$n_h), "\n")
```

# Sample size versus margin of error

The next graph shows how the required total sample size changes as the target confidence-interval half-width changes.

```{r margin-grid}
margin_grid <- seq(2, 15, by = 0.25)

required_n <- sapply(
  margin_grid,
  function(e) find_min_strat_n(e, N_h, S_h, z)$n
)

sample_size_curve <- data.frame(
  margin_of_error = margin_grid,
  required_sample_size = required_n
)

head(sample_size_curve)
```

```{r sample-size-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
plot(
  sample_size_curve$margin_of_error,
  sample_size_curve$required_sample_size,
  type = "l",
  lwd = 2,
  xlab = "Confidence-interval half-width (pages)",
  ylab = "Required total sample size",
  main = "Required Sample Size versus Margin of Error"
)

abline(v = E, lty = 2)
abline(h = n_strat, lty = 2)

points(E, n_strat, pch = 19)
```

# Sensitivity analysis: 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% of baseline

The assignment also requires the sample-size calculation to be repeated for assumed parameter values equal to 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% of the baseline value.

For each assumed parameter value, the margin of error is expressed as a percentage of that assumed parameter value. The population size, faculty sizes, stratum weights, stratum standard deviations, confidence level, sampling design and Neyman allocation rule are held fixed.

```{r sensitivity-values}
baseline_fractions <- c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00)

assumed_means <- baseline_mean * baseline_fractions

sensitivity_table <- data.frame(
  baseline_fraction = baseline_fractions,
  assumed_parameter = assumed_means,
  five_percent_halfwidth = 0.05 * assumed_means
)

sensitivity_table
```

Calculate the sample size required at the 5% precision level for each assumed parameter value.

```{r sensitivity-n}
sensitivity_table$required_n <- sapply(
  sensitivity_table$five_percent_halfwidth,
  function(e) find_min_strat_n(e, N_h, S_h, z)$n
)

sensitivity_table
```

# Four sensitivity curves on one graph

To show how required sample size changes with precision, margins of error from 2% to 15% of each assumed parameter value are considered.

```{r sensitivity-curves-data}
relative_margins <- seq(0.02, 0.15, by = 0.005)

curve_list <- lapply(
  seq_along(assumed_means),
  function(j) {
    assumed_value <- assumed_means[j]

    absolute_margins <- relative_margins * assumed_value

    n_values <- sapply(
      absolute_margins,
      function(e) find_min_strat_n(e, N_h, S_h, z)$n
    )

    data.frame(
      relative_margin_percent = 100 * relative_margins,
      absolute_margin = absolute_margins,
      required_n = n_values,
      assumed_parameter = assumed_value,
      baseline_fraction = baseline_fractions[j]
    )
  }
)

sensitivity_curves <- do.call(rbind, curve_list)
```

```{r four-curves-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
curve_25 <- subset(sensitivity_curves, baseline_fraction == 0.25)
curve_50 <- subset(sensitivity_curves, baseline_fraction == 0.50)
curve_75 <- subset(sensitivity_curves, baseline_fraction == 0.75)
curve_100 <- subset(sensitivity_curves, baseline_fraction == 1.00)

ylim_values <- range(sensitivity_curves$required_n)

plot(
  curve_25$relative_margin_percent,
  curve_25$required_n,
  type = "l",
  lwd = 2,
  ylim = ylim_values,
  xlab = "Margin of error (% of assumed parameter value)",
  ylab = "Required total sample size",
  main = "Sample-Size Sensitivity to Assumed Parameter Value"
)

lines(
  curve_50$relative_margin_percent,
  curve_50$required_n,
  lwd = 2,
  lty = 2
)

lines(
  curve_75$relative_margin_percent,
  curve_75$required_n,
  lwd = 2,
  lty = 3
)

lines(
  curve_100$relative_margin_percent,
  curve_100$required_n,
  lwd = 2,
  lty = 4
)

abline(v = 5, lty = 2)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c(
    "25% of baseline",
    "50% of baseline",
    "75% of baseline",
    "100% of baseline"
  ),
  lty = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  lwd = 2,
  bty = "n"
)
```

# Quantities held fixed in the sensitivity analysis

The following quantities are held fixed:

* finite population size, 
* five faculty population sizes
* stratum-specific standard deviations
* 95% confidence level;
* stratified random sampling without replacement;
* Neyman allocation rule; and
* the simulated finite-population structure.

Only the assumed value of the primary parameter, and therefore the absolute margin of error associated with a specified relative precision, is changed.

# Comparison with the SRSWOR benchmark

```{r comparison}
comparison <- data.frame(
  Design = c(
    "SRSWOR benchmark",
    "Stratified Neyman (minimum completed sample)",
    "Stratified Neyman (10% non-response adjusted)"
  ),
  Sample_size = c(
    n_srs,
    n_strat,
    n_final
  )
)

comparison
```
